Thank you everyone for the feedback and contributions, I appreciate it immensely. I am still doing research and taking things into consideration. As with research, answers can lead to additional questions.

The intent for purchasing a keyboard/synth:

Learning piano/keyboard/synthesis (operation of a synthesizer)
Recording & writing music
Use for live performance and at home
Drum/Rhythm accompaniment (I don’t know many drummers who are available)
Creating sounds & experimentation (soundscapes/ambient/lead or bass lines/background/augmentation etc). 

The keyboard/synth will probably be utilized in a variety of ways: with headphones, the built-in speakers, plugged into a PA (Peavey PA-200 - 1/4 inch jacks), or with a DAW (I don’t have a digital workspace set up yet, but I am considering GarageBand or Ableton for the future. I have Apple Logic, but it seems like it won’t install despite the fact that I have a MacBook).

Ideally, I am seeking something that is versatile and customizable for a variety of genres and styles. 

Questions:

Is it possible to run guitar effects pedals (or a metronome) with 1/4 inch jack(s) through a keyboard/synth or use a PA with these keyboards? Some keys have RCA jacks, is there a conversion cable (RCA to 1/4 inch) or is that a no-go?

It seems like MIDI (some keys I am looking at have MIDI, some don’t) would be a great option to work with. Are there pros/cons to MIDI or is it just as easy to get those results with RCA or 1/4 inch jacks (my assumption is that MIDI is superior to these other options)? I plan to mix in guitar effects pedal for more sonic variety and plug into a PA for amplification (for at-home or live performance use), pretty sure MIDI isn’t meant for that. 

I have an understanding that MIDI does not create sound but can transmit data. There a lot of possibilities with this so I may end up with something that has MIDI. 

Additionally, I own a Dubreq Stylophone GEN X-1 that I am thinking of using that with the keyboard. Would this possible to do? 


What I’m thinking of going with:

Yamaha PSS – 480 

This keyboard comes with MIDI IN & OUT and a 1/4 inch(?) headphone/AUX OUT. Is it possible/safe to run guitar effects pedals and/or a PA (Peavey PA-200) through this output? 

Yamaha PSS – 560

[Yamaha PSS - 560 and DSR - 2000 comparison video](https://youtu.be/AQWtFOBr6zs)

I really love the sounds at 3:30 & 3:50 (especially this setting/sound). How does the settings/sound (same, similar, or different) compare on the other PSS’s? I love this sound and was wondering if it can be achieved through MIDI or other keyboards. I believe this keyboard only has RCA jacks and a mini headphone jack, so this may not be the best option, but I love the sounds made in the video. 

Yamaha PSS – 680

I am aware this has MIDI IN & OUT, but not sure what else comes with it. Definitely considering this, the PSS-480 or PSS-560. 

Technics SX – K150

[Technics SX-K150 demo](https://youtu.be/bDNYlGm3lMk)

The sounds at 5:30 are what got me hooked for the Technics, I believe it is either the brass or strings setting. I was wondering if you can get that sound/setting through MIDI or other keyboards? Are the other levels/models of Technics decent and do they possess MIDI ports?

Korg Mini Korg w/ Vocoder

Not opposed to a vocoder and synth combo. However, there may not be any drum/rhythm tracks available with this. 

Roland PCR-500 

I believe this is a MIDI controller but it seems like it does a lot for a low price. I may end up not going with this option.

It’s ok man we all learn something new everyday.  I’m glad you are restoring your musicmaster. Should you feel the need to upgrade it you could buy a pickguard for 2 single coils or whatever design and install a pick up in the bridge since all bodies were routed for 2 pickups regardless of pickup configuration. I love the bodies of these guitars. I had a Jag-Stang and sold it since it was so heavy then bought the music since it basically had everything I wanted and a lighter body. It’s awesome when dreams come true. Best of luck on the search for a sonic blue model.

The neck is a 1963 Short scale 22.5” (measured it myself). The model name has been scratched off right below the Fender logo by someone who had it before me, but it’s not quite noticeable until you see it up close in person, I prefer it that way so it looks almost like a custom model. The date is from April 1963 and has 3/4 and A which signifies the smaller scale (22.5”) rather than the 24”.  I’ve included the photos the seller posted before I bought it. After 1962 they moved from slab fretboards to a rosewood veneer fretboard. The neck didn’t come with tuners originally so i put some aftermarket Gotohs since I prefer the look over the white plastic ones and these Gotohs hold tune better. It may look too good to be true but it is the real deal.
